title: Sub-second dopamine reinforcement shapes juvenile social play
title_zh: 亚秒级多巴胺强化塑造青少年社交游戏
abstract: Juvenile social play is critical for neurodevelopment, yet the neural mechanisms organizing moment-to-moment interactions remain elusive. Using social behavior sequencing (Social-seq)-an occlusion-robust 3D pose estimation and unsupervised clustering pipeline-we found that nucleus accumbens (NAc) dopamine was tightly coupled to sub-second social syllables during naturalistic interactions. In wild-type juveniles, males exhibited a sharper dopaminergic contrast between proactive play and forced submission than females did, consistent with sex-divergent play strategies. In Shank3-deficient autism models, this process was fundamentally corrupted: proactive play-evoked dopamine responses were abolished in males and significantly sign-inverted in females, with male-specific enhancements during non-social behaviors, driving social play deficits. A multi-agent reinforcement learning model parameterized by disrupted, play-related dopaminergic reinforcement values recapitulated mutant phenotypes. Closed-loop optogenetic stimulation of ventral tegmental area (VTA)-NAc dopamine projections, time-locked to proactive play, restored reciprocal play in Shank3-deficient rats. Sub-second dopaminergic reinforcement thus orchestrates naturalistic social behavior, providing a behaviorally contingent interventional framework for neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract_zh: 青少年社交游戏对神经发育至关重要，但组织瞬时互动的神经机制仍难以捉摸。利用社交行为测序（Social-seq）——一种对遮挡具有鲁棒性的三维姿态估计与无监督聚类流水线——我们发现，伏隔核（NAc）多巴胺与自然互动中的亚秒级社交音节紧密耦合。在野生型青少年中，雄性在主动游戏与被动屈服之间表现出比雌性更明显的多巴胺对比度，符合性别异质的游戏策略。在Shank3缺陷的自闭症模型中，这一过程根本性地被破坏：雄性的主动游戏诱发的多巴胺反应被消除，雌性的反应显著符号反转，且雄性在非社交行为期间出现特异性增强，导致社交游戏缺陷。基于被破坏的与游戏相关的多巴胺强化值参数化的多智能体增强学习模型复现了突变体表型。锁定在主动游戏时间的腹侧被盖区（VTA）-NAc多巴胺投射闭环光遗传刺激恢复了Shank3缺陷大鼠的互惠性游戏。因此，亚秒级多巴胺强化调控自然社交行为，为神经发育障碍提供了基于行为依赖性的干预框架。
